title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a page of Grothendieck's 1981 work on dessins d'enfants. It treats the variant with orientation removed, where complex conjugation is allowed to act. The previous page introduced the 'mixed' fundamental group Pi_{0,3}^tau = pi_1(U_{0,3}, {1,tau}; P_+). Here U_{0,3} = P^1(C) minus {0,1,infinity}, tau is complex conjugation and P_+ is a base point in the upper half-plane. This is the fundamental group of the orbifold quotient U_{0,3}(C)/<tau>, an extension of Z/2 by the free group F_2. Joining P_- = tau(P_+) to P_+ by half great circles lambda_i through the real points Q_i (Q_1 = -1, Q_0 = 2, Q_infinity = 1/2) gives three involutions tau_i = (lambda_i, tau). These generate Pi_{0,3}^tau, which is isomorphic to the free product Z/2*Z/2*Z/2, the extended (infinity, infinity, infinity) triangle group.

This page states the following.
(1) The category (up to isotopy) of finite weighted triangulated maps of type {0,1,infinity} is equivalent to a full subcategory of finite étale {1,tau}-coverings of U_{0,3}. These are covers U' -> U_{0,3} with an antiholomorphic involution lifting conjugation; equivalently, finite Pi^tau-sets. The subcategory is cut out by an extra condition: the three involutions tau_0, tau_1, tau_infinity act without fixed points, i.e. flag sets with free involutions, which means surfaces without boundary.
(2) He reinterprets this condition. For any {1,tau}-covering, the fixed points of tau_i correspond to the connected components of U'^tau lying over the arc of U_{0,3}(R) opposite P_i, i.e. the arc containing Q_i. So the condition is (25): U'^tau is empty, equivalently X'^tau is empty, where X' is the ramified cover of P^1(C) extending U'.
(3) First NB: X'^tau is a closed real-analytic curve in X'. Hence it is empty as soon as its trace on U' (X' minus the ramification points) is empty.
(4) Second NB: in terms of the original map, X' is the double cover of local orientations of the map's surface. tau_{X'} is the deck involution reversing orientation, which is indeed fixed-point-free.
(5) He then starts the general statement, without condition (25). A {1,tau}-ramified covering of Sigma = P^1(C), étale over U_{0,3}, is the same as a C/R descent datum. This yields (next page) an equivalence with ramified covers of P^1_R étale over P^1_R minus {0,1,infinity}. It also yields a fully faithful functor from weighted maps (no boundary, possibly non-orientable) to such real covers, with essential image the covers with X'(R) empty.

In modern terms this is real Belyi / Klein-surface dessin theory. Maps on arbitrary compact surfaces correspond to real algebraic curves with a Belyi map defined over R. Maps on closed surfaces correspond to real curves without real points (closed orientable or non-orientable surfaces arising as X'(C)/tau). The real locus corresponds exactly to the boundary of the map, arc by arc over the three real intervals.
errors: No mathematical error. The NB is correct and could be sharpened: the fixed locus of an antiholomorphic involution on a compact Riemann surface is a disjoint union of circles with no isolated points, so it cannot be hidden in the finite ramification set.
Minor terminological looseness: the map side ('cartes triangulaires pondérées') implicitly allows non-orientable surfaces. The free action of the tau_i encodes 'no boundary', not orientability.

ideas.what: Mixed fundamental group pi_1(U_{0,3},{1,tau}) of P^1 minus 3 points with complex conjugation, generated by three involutions; finite sets with its action correspond to maps on arbitrary (possibly non-orientable, bordered) surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Extended triangle group / non-oriented cartographic group; orbifold fundamental group of U_{0,3}(C)/conj; topological part of pi_1^et(P^1_R minus 3 points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bryant-Singerman (1985, maps on surfaces with boundary); Jones-Singerman (1994); Grothendieck, Esquisse (non-oriented cartographic group)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of non-oriented maps and the cartographic group generated by involutions

ideas.what: Fixed points of tau_i (i.e. boundary flags) correspond to connected components of the real locus lying over the real arc opposite to the i-th point
ideas.modern_name: Boundary of a real dessin = real locus of the real Belyi curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Köck-Singerman, 'Real Belyi theory' (2007); Singerman's work on Klein surfaces

ideas.what: Maps without boundary correspond to real Belyi covers with X'(R) empty; X' is the orientation double cover with free orientation-reversing involution
ideas.modern_name: Dessins on closed (non-orientable) Klein surfaces ↔ real curves without real points; complex double of a Klein surface

ideas.what: {1,tau}-equivariant ramified covers of P^1(C) = C/R descent data, giving an equivalence with covers of P^1_R étale over P^1_R minus {0,1,infinity}
ideas.modern_name: Galois descent for real algebraic curves (Weil descent C/R)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (descent); the application to maps is sketched in the Esquisse

missed.claim: An explicit 1981 dictionary between non-oriented maps (with or without boundary) and real Belyi covers. Components of X'(R) over each of the three real arcs correspond to tau_i-fixed flags. Boundaryless maps correspond to covers with X'(R) empty, via the orientation double cover. This anticipates the 'real Belyi theory' of Köck-Singerman (2007), which is usually not credited to Grothendieck beyond the Esquisse's brief remarks.
missed.quote: les points fixes des τ_i correspondent aux composantes connexes de U^τ qui sont au-dessus de l'arc de U_{0,3}(ℝ) opposé à P_i ... (25) U'^τ = ∅ i.e. X'^τ = ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for real/Klein-surface dessin theory. The result itself is now known, so the mathematical novelty is small.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a correct, careful early version of real Belyi theory: boundary corresponds to real locus, closed surfaces to curves without real points. It is partly sketched in the Esquisse and fully developed later by Singerman and coauthors. The page offers a mild priority detail, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'cartes (bi-maillées[?])' is probably 'cartes (triangulées)'; the next page says 'cartes triangulaires'.
'composantes connexes de U^τ' should be U'^τ (the cover, not the base).
'sa trace sur U' = X' [-ramifié-]' means U' = X' minus the ramification points; read 'X' − (pts de ramification)'.
First line: 'les catégories isotopiques des cartes'; the inserted word 'isotopiques' replaces a struck-out word.
